summary: Two blockers found. (1) CompatibilityGuard is always rendered with error={null} — the structured MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH error UI (showing group-per-product breakdown) is dead code; only a generic string error reaches users. (2) The client-side compatibility filter in IngredientPicker uses consumptionClassification (food/non-food/caution) instead of the server's mixingGroup; the Product type doesn't even expose mixingGroup to the web client, so the picker cannot be mixing-group-aware as required. Also HIGH: acceptance criterion 7 says files should be removed but PowderizerActions.tsx, powderizerRandom.ts, powderizerCopy.ts (contains comedic copy like 'Hairy legs', 'Tax avoidance'), IngredientReaction.tsx, DailyRecipeCard.tsx, and the old history stack all remain on disk.

evidence_assessment.notes: Reproduced: 10 files, 41 tests, all pass at 20:42 UTC

findings.title: CompatibilityGuard always receives error={null} — server-crafted MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH structured errors never rendered

trace.input: Server returns a MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH error body conforming to IncompatibleGroupError shape from contracts (conflictingProductIds + groupInfo per product)
trace.state: PowderizerPage.tsx:136 renders <CompatibilityGuard error={null} productNamesById={namesByProductId} />. The controller usePowderizerController.ts:87-100 passes all quote errors through messageFor() which only captures error.message as a string. The structured IncompatibleGroupError data is never extracted from the API response.
trace.wrong_output: CompatibilityGuard returns null (line 10: if (!error) return null). Only the generic string error appears in the quote error section (lines 117-128). Users never see which specific products conflict or their mixing group names. The rich structured UI in CompatibilityGuard (lines 12-39) showing per-product group labels is dead code.

findings.remediation: In the controller, catch API errors that carry IncompatibleGroupError body, extract to state, pass through to CompatibilityGuard instead of hardcoded null.

findings.title: Client-side compatibility filter uses consumptionClassification, not mixingGroup — picker is not mixing-group-aware

trace.input: Products have both consumptionClassification (optional on Product type: 'food'|'non-food'|'caution') and mixingGroup (only on ProductWithVariants type, absent from Product base type). Server validates mixingGroup on quote.
trace.state: IngredientPicker.tsx:14-27 builds selectedGroups from product.consumptionClassification. IngredientPicker.tsx:62-66 checks isIncompatible using selectedGroups.has(product.consumptionClassification). The Product type (products.ts:95) does NOT expose mixingGroup — only ProductWithVariants:392 does. The text label at IngredientPicker.tsx:76 says 'different mix group' but the underlying check is on consumption classification.
trace.wrong_output: (a) Products with same consumptionClassification but different mixingGroup pass client guard → server rejects → confusing UX. (b) Products with different consumptionClassification but same mixingGroup are blocked → false restriction. (c) The UI label 'different mix group' is misleading — it's consumption classification filtering, not mixing group.

findings.remediation: Either expose mixingGroup on Product type returned from config endpoint and switch the filter to use it, or rename the filter to consumption-classification-based and update labels. The acceptance criterion explicitly calls for 'mixing-group-aware picker' so the first option is the intended fix.

findings.title: Files marked for removal by acceptance criterion 7 still exist on disk, including comedic fixture content

trace.input: Acceptance criterion 7: 'Removed: PowderizerActions, powderizerRandom, powderizerCopy, IngredientReaction, DailyRecipeCard, Chaos Mix'
trace.state: All listed files still exist: powderizer/Actions.tsx (Chaos Mix button), powderizer/powderizerRandom.ts+test.ts (chaosMixBuilderConfig, isChaosPoolFeasible), powderizer/powderizerCopy.ts+test.ts (selectGoodFor with comedic options: 'Hairy legs', 'Tax avoidance', 'Negotiating raises', 'Avoiding small talk', etc.; selectIngredientReaction with 'Housewarming achieved. Keep away from actual flames.' etc.), powderizer/IngredientReaction.tsx, powderizer/DailyRecipeCard.tsx. Additionally, the old history stack remains: powderizer/usePowderizerHistory.ts (imports selectGoodFor), powderizer/powderizerHistory.ts, powderizer/PowderizerHistoryShelf.tsx. powderizerState.test.ts and PowderizerPresentation.test.tsx still import from powderizerCopy.ts and IngredientReaction.tsx respectively.
trace.wrong_output: Competent/humorous content persists in the codebase. Risk: future developer re-imports these as legitimate utilities. Deleting requires updating the two test files that still import from them.

findings.remediation: Delete the listed files and the old history stack. Update powderizerState.test.ts (remove selectGoodFor import and dependent tests) and PowderizerPresentation.test.tsx (remove IngredientReaction tests).

findings.title: No test coverage for mixing-group-aware picker or server MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH error rendering

trace.input: Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 require: (2) mixing-group-aware picker with accessible explanation, (3) server-crafted MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH errors rendered to user.
trace.state: Test fixtures in PowderizerPage.test.tsx and PowderizerHistoryPage.test.tsx do not set consumptionClassification or mixingGroup on products, so the IngredientPicker incompatibility filter never activates in tests. No test simulates a server MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH error response. No test verifies that the accessible explanation (aria-describedby on disabled incompatible button) is rendered.
trace.wrong_output: Both acceptance criteria are untested. A regression in the compatibility filter would not be caught. The blocker F1 (CompatibilityGuard always null) could have been caught by a test.

findings.remediation: Add: (a) test with products having different consumptionClassifications to verify disabled+incompatible state and accessible explanation; (b) test simulating a MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH error from the API and verifying it renders via CompatibilityGuard with per-product group info.

findings.title: Disabled incompatible button explanation not accessible to screen readers

trace.input: A product is incompatible with the current selection. The button is rendered disabled with aria-describedby pointing to a hidden <span> explaining the incompatibility.
trace.state: IngredientPicker.tsx:84 sets disabled={selected || isAtMaximum || isIncompatible} on the Button. The Button component renders a native HTML <button disabled> element. Disabled buttons are removed from the tab order by the browser. The aria-describedby on line 86 references a hidden <span> (line 91-93), but screen readers only announce aria-describedby when the element receives focus — which a disabled button never does.
trace.wrong_output: Screen reader users navigating via Tab skip all disabled incompatible buttons. The accessible explanation 'This product belongs to a different mixing group than your selected powders' is never read. Only sighted users see the visual 'Incompatible' label and the '— different mix group' text.

findings.remediation: Use aria-disabled='true' instead of disabled, or surface the explanation as visible adjacent text with an accessible name, or use a tooltip/aria-live region for screen reader users.

observations_notes: Navigation label still reads 'Powderizer' in CategoryNav (navItems.ts:32) — not covered by acceptance criteria 1 (headings/actions/history only) but inconsistent with the new 'Custom Powder' heading.
cryptoRandom() still exported from usePowderizerController.ts:36-39 with comment 'Only used by legacy fallback components' — should be removed once legacy files are deleted.
No /custom-powder web route or alias/redirect loop exists — route is /powderizer rendering PowderizerPage directly. No compatible-alias-loop risk.
History migration from OLD_HISTORY_KEY correctly discards goodFor field from old entries — verified by PowderizerHistoryPage.test.tsx:238.
